items.title: Дослідження впливу AI-асистованого прийняття рішень на ефективність виявлення дефектів у процесі тестування програмного забезпечення в Agile-командах
items.abstract: Стаття аналізує взаємодію людини та систем штучного інтелекту (ШІ, AI) у тестуванні програмного забезпечення в Agile-командах. Досліджено вплив AI-асистованого прийняття рішень на ефективність виявлення дефектів, швидкість тестування та якість командної роботи. Проведено огляд сучасних наукових джерел щодо використання ШІ в тестуванні, автоматизації контролю якості та впливу AI-інструментів на діяльність тестувальників у багатофункціональних командах. Визначено переваги й ризики застосування AI-асистованих систем: автоматизаційне упередження, надмірна довіра до AI-рекомендацій, зниження критичного мислення тестувальників, можливість хибнопозитивних результатів. Досліджено особливості Human-AI Collaboration у тестуванні, визначено ключові фактори результативності AI-асистованого тестування в Agile-середовищах. Проведено емпіричне дослідження із залученням тестувальників, які використовували AI-інструменти для генерації тестових сценаріїв, аналізу дефектів і підтримки прийняття рішень. Встановлено, що AI-асистовані підходи підвищують швидкість виявлення дефектів і оптимізують тестування, але потребують постійного людського контролю та перевірки рекомендацій. Запропоновано рекомендації щодо ефективної інтеграції AI-інструментів у тестування в Agile-командах. Результати мають практичне значення для організації процесів забезпечення якості програмного забезпечення та розробки нових підходів до управління Human-AI взаємодією у сфері тестування.

items.abstract: The article examines the significance of contemporary realities and challenges that impose new demands on the personality of higher education faculty members. It is noted that a university lecturer acts as an intermediary between socio-economic needs and state requirements—focused on training future professionals for Ukraine’s post-war reconstruction—and the shaping of the self-awareness and national culture of modern society. The article emphasizes that the lecturer's capacity for self-organization is a key factor in overcoming the challenges of the current academic landscape, a quality that takes on particular importance in developing a culture of academic governance. An analytical synthesis of approaches to understanding the self-organization of higher education faculty within the context of corporate culture has been conducted; empirical data regarding the key characteristics of faculty professional self-organization, considering the specific features of corporate culture, have been analyzed. The professional self-organization of a higher education faculty member is conceptualized as a process of cultivating internal motivation, discipline, and the refinement of professional personal attributes—a process accompanied by self-awareness, focus, goal-orientation, and professional competence; the mobilization of all intellectual resources and their practical application within the educational environment; the establishment of fundamental principles of ethics and integrity in organizational communication; and the articulation of a shared vision and its realization through the lens of a specific academic community's corporate culture. The study employed the expert assessment method to identify the priority characteristics of professional self-organization, utilizing a custom-designed questionnaire, interviews, and a survey of expert respondents. Based on the analysis of empirical data, the priority characteristics of professional self-organization were identified as follows: "professional competencies," "awareness of set goals," "intrinsic motivation," "professional development," and "self-realization." The findings can be used to further develop indicators and assessment methodologies to track the dynamics of components of a higher education lecturer's professional self-organization as it develops and is actualized.

items.abstract: The article discusses the methodological foundations of compliance with ethical standards when using artificial intelligence technologies in the educational process. The relevance of the study is due to the widespread introduction of AI into educational practice and the need to form a responsible attitude of students to its use. The paper analyzes theoretical approaches to understanding the ethical principles of using artificial intelligence, including issues of Academic Integrity, Protection of personal data and Prevention of misinformation. Particular attention is paid to the development and testing of a system of educational tasks aimed at developing students ' skills for critical analysis of content created using artificial intelligence, as well as the formation of skills for safe and ethically justified use of digital technologies. As part of the study, methods of pedagogical observation, survey, analysis of the results of educational activities and pedagogical experiment were used. The results of the study showed that the introduction of specially developed methodological approaches contributes to increasing the level of digital literacy, the development of critical thinking and the formation of sustainable skills for the ethical use of artificial intelligence tools. The obtained conclusions can be used in the development of educational programs and methodological recommendations for teachers.

items.abstract: The purpose of this article is to present more fundamentally the natural metabolism of science and the scientific journal, partly using examples from radiology. The journal article is the main tool and practice of the researcher in converting personal knowledge into public knowledge for its verification and pragmatic realization. In national medicine and radiology, there is a problem of long-term preservation of knowledge (the work of scientists and state finances) and its accessibility against the backdrop of the emergence of new journals and their disappearance. If earlier there was a problem with the publication of articles due to the shortage of journals and the queue for publication, now there is a problem with the shortage of high-quality content articles. Virtually all significant results in the exact sciences (at least in the English-speaking world) can be found in the pages of just two journals: “Nature” and “Science”. Lotka’s law is mentioned in the aspect of the scientific literature citation system as a means of tracking the development of science. Attention is drawn to the formation of a new subspecialty – medical writers (since 1940). The replication crisis is described (possibly caused by human factors), a methodological crisis in which the results of many scientific studies are difficult or impossible to reproduce. The mobilization of science in the journal “Radiation diagnostics, radiation therapy” during the COVID-19 pandemic is considered using the example of articles “Low-dose radiation therapy for COVID-19 pneumonia”, “COVID-modulated emphysematous pyelonephritis against the background of severe course of oxygen-dependent covid pneumonia” та “Echocardiographic characteristics of complicated course of coronavirus infection in children (COVID-19) (review and portfolio)”. The bibliometrics of the journal “Radiology” (journal of the Radiological Society of North America.) are presented for comparison: the most viewed articles of 2021 and the most cited articles of 2021. It is demonstrated that the topic of the most cited articles of 2023 is artificial intelligence.

items.abstract: The article substantiates the concept of national resilience as an emerging governance paradigm within Ukraine's state security system. Drawing on an analysis of NATO, EU, and International Organization for Standardization standards, as well as Ukrainian strategic documents, the study elucidates the distinctions between the traditional "security" paradigm and the dynamic paradigm of "resilience". The paper proposes institutional mechanisms for interagency coordination, algorithms for establishing unified situational awareness, and protocols for subsidiarity-based response and public-private partnership. It is demonstrated that resilience functions as an integrated framework for managing challenges and threats under conditions of hybrid warfare. The scientific novelty lies in the development of a matrix model for coordinating security actors that incorporates a network-centric approach into public administration. The practical significance is reflected in the applicability of the proposed mechanisms for assessing the resilience levels of public administration sectors, critical infrastructure, and cybersecurity.

items.abstract: The article explores metacognitive approaches to teaching Abai’s Words of Edification based on the Mürseyit manuscripts and emphasizes their role in developing students’ cognitive and reflective abilities. The relevance of the study lies in the need to foster metacognitive skills in higher education through the conscious study of Abai’s literary heritage using authentic manuscript sources. This approach promotes deeper text comprehension, independent reasoning, self-regulation, and objective self-assessment while enhancing students’ scientific and cognitive competencies. The purpose of the study is to identify effective methods of organizing students’ learning activities through the metacognitive teaching of Abai’s Words of Edification using the Mürseyit manuscripts. Particular attention is paid to the comparative analysis of manuscript texts for interpreting the philosophical and educational ideas of Abai and stimulating students’ cognitive engagement. The research employed comparative analysis, empirical methods, questionnaire survey, and statistical analysis. The survey was conducted among 62 second- and third-year students of Khoja Akhmet Yassawi International Kazakh-Turkish University to examine their perceptions of learning Abai’s Words of Edification through the Mürseyit manuscripts. The collected data were processed using SPSS Statistics 26. The findings indicate that teaching Abai’s Words of Edification through the Mürseyit manuscripts contributes to deeper text comprehension, stronger analytical thinking, and the development of metacognitive skills. The proposed methodological framework supports students in planning, monitoring, and evaluating their learning activities while encouraging informed selection of learning strategies. The study has both scientific and practical significance by advancing literary education and demonstrating the effectiveness of integrating metacognitive approaches into the teaching of Abai’s works in higher education.

items.abstract: The article presents the results of an empirical study examining the use of large language models by first-year non-philology students during foreign language learning. The aim of the study is to investigate the frequency, patterns, purposes, and motivations behind students' use of large language models who are not majoring in a foreign language. The empirical basis of the study consists of survey results from 51 respondents in March 2026. The collected data were analyzed using both quantitative and qualitative research methods. The survey revealed that ChatGPT and Gemini are the most widely used large language models among students. The paper found that more than one-quarter of respondents use large language models daily for educational purposes. The primary motivation for using these tools is time efficiency and the desire to complete academic tasks more quickly, regardless of subject complexity. Large language models are most frequently employed for vocabulary and text translation, grammar explanation, and the completion of lexical-grammar exercises and tests. However, their potential for developing productive language skills, particularly speaking and listening, remains underutilized. The study also revealed that most students are aware that using large language models may lead to violations of academic integrity principles. At the same time, the findings suggest that students do not always have a clear understanding of the boundaries between acceptable and unacceptable uses of artificial intelligence tools in academic contexts. Based on the results obtained, methodological recommendations are proposed for integrating large language models into foreign language instruction, including the use of Text-to-Speech technologies, elements of the flipped classroom approach, and creative communicative tasks in which large language models serve as supportive learning tools.

items.abstract: This article examines the pragmatic strategies used to create a comic effect in English- and Kazakh-language stand-up comedy, drawing on performances by Dave Chappelle and Tursynbek Kabatov. The relevance of the study is determined by the growing scholarly interest in humorous discourse as a distinct type of verbal interaction reflecting social, cultural and cognitive processes. The aim of the research is to reveal the mechanisms of humor generation through the violation of P. Grice’s cooperative maxims (quality, quantity, relevance and manner) the deliberate flouting of which functions as a key mechanism for forming implicatures and stimulating the audience’s cognitive engagement. The empirical basis of the study comprises transcribed and qualitatively analyzed video recordings of stand-up performances. The findings show that Dave Chappell more frequently employs hyperbole, sarcasm, intertextual allusions and obscene vocabulary to emphasize social and racial contradictions, whereas Tursynbek Kabatov relies on conversational redundancy, pleonasms, thematic shifts and code-mixing, thereby creating an atmosphere of everyday irony and cultural intimacy with the audience. It has been established that intentional violations of the cooperative maxims do not disrupt communication but rather promote the emergence of implicatures that engage listeners in interpretive activity and intensify the comic effect. The scholarly contribution of this work lies in demonstrating the universality of Grice’s cooperative principles within humorous discourse while identifying nationally specific ways of its violation that shape each comedian’s individual style. The practical significance of the research consists in the potential application of its results to the analysis and teaching of pragmatics, sociolinguistics and intercultural communication. Thus, stand-up comedy appears nor merely as a genre of entertainment discourse, but also as a mean of sociocultural reflection.

items.abstract: The paper substantiates the theoretical foundations of trauma-informed education in a digital educational environment under the conditions of cognitive-information influences. The relevance stems from the fact that under conditions of prolonged military and information pressure, digital platforms that ensure the continuity of the educational process simultaneously become channels for the dissemination of emotionally charged, shocking, and traumatic content. Under such circumstances, the digital educational environment acquires the characteristics not only of a technical infrastructure for learning but also of a sociotechnical space where didactic opportunities, information threats, and psycho-emotional risks for both students and educators converge. The purpose of the paper is to substantiate the theoretical foundations of trauma-informed education in a digital educational environment during hybrid warfare by systematizing the conceptual field of the study, analysing the interconnections between war, media, and information technologies. The study is theoretical and analytical in nature, based on conceptual, comparative-analytical, systems analysis, systematization of scientific findings, and theoretical modelling. The study differentiates between war as a general reality and a source of direct traumatic experience, cognitive warfare as a targeted impact on perception, emotional responses, trust, and behaviour, and media-induced traumatization as a broader psycho-emotional phenomenon. The digital educational environment is characterized as a sociotechnical space combining didactic resources, information influences, and psycho-emotional risks. War, media, and information technologies form a shared field of influence that alters the conditions of the educational process and necessitates a trauma-informed approach. The theoretical framework of trauma-informed education is multi-component and includes trauma-sensitive, psycho-emotional safety, information-hygiene, digital-resilience, ethical-communicative, and adaptive-pedagogical components. Based on the findings, the general guidelines for adapting pedagogical practice to the conditions of intensive media influence, algorithmically reinforced content pressure, and psycho-emotional tension are outlined. Trauma-informed education in a digital educational environment serves as a promising theoretical and practical basis for reimagining pedagogical interaction under the conditions of cognitive-information influences.

items.abstract: The article presents the results of a study addressing the challenges associated with organizing and maintaining interoperability between units of the State Border Guard Service of Ukraine (SBGSU) and other components of the Defense Forces of Ukraine under the conditions of full-scale armed aggression. Based on an analysis of existing scientific and methodological materials, as well as operational and combat experience gained during 2022–2025, practical recommendations are proposed for implementing the modular organizational framework and integrating automated situational awareness systems (the Delta system) into this framework. These measures are considered key factors in achieving the required levels of adequacy and responsiveness in organizing interoperability among SBGSU forces and assets while performing missions as part of the Defense Forces under martial law.

items.title: Язык образовательных инноваций как «праксема»: семиотика трансформаций городской среды в концепциях «город-университет»
items.abstract: Современное развитие территорий (городов) и университетов, движимое технократической логикой эффективности и инноваций, порождает риск утраты человеческого измерения. Расширяется трактовка образовательной инновации, включая в неё инфраструктуру искусственного интеллекта, что позволяет рассматривать университеты в качестве активных семиотических агентов, внедряющих эти инновации в урбанистический контекст. Цель исследования заключается в разработке и апробации методологии сравнительного семиотического анализа образовательных инноваций как инструмента трансформации городской среды в концепции «город-университет». Актуальность работы обусловлена доминированием технократической парадигмы во взаимодействии вузов и городов, что порождает риск «гуманитарного дефицита» – утраты субъектности человека и его смыслообразующей роли в образовании и урбанистическом развитии. Теоретико-методологической основой выступают: концепт «праксема» (С. С. Аванесов); подход Г. Н. Прозументовой, акцентирующий феномен «личного присутствия» и преодоление антропологического дефицита через субъективацию образования; концепция «семиотической диагностики» (И. В. Мелик-Гайказян), предлагающая паллиативное решение проблемы измерения в гуманитарных исследованиях. Исследование доказывает, что язык образовательных инноваций является критически важным фактором и индикатором гуманитарного качества трансформаций в рамках концепций «город-университет». Его анализ позволяет не только диагностировать текущие изменения, но и прогнозировать их антропологические последствия, открывая перспективы для управления развитием территорий не только как технологических, но и как подлинно человеческих, смыслонасыщенных пространств. Научная значимость исследования состоит в том, что устанавливается связь между концептом «праксема» и концепцией «семиотической диагностики» и в опоре на эту связь предлагается конкретный способ перехода от измерения количественных показателей эффективности к анализу глубинных антропологических эффектов образовательных инноваций и выявлению рисков символической дегуманизации в концепциях «город-университет». The study emphasizes that the contemporary development of territories (cities) and universities, driven by the technocratic logic of efficiency and innovation, generates the risk of losing the human dimension. The aim of the research is to develop and test a methodology of comparative semiotic analysis of educational innovations as a tool for transforming the urban environment within the “city-university” concept. The relevance of the work is determined by the dominance of the technocratic paradigm in the interaction between universities and cities, which creates the risk of a “humanitarian deficit” — the loss of human subjectivity and its meaning-forming role in education and urban development. The theoretical basis of the study is the concept of the “praxema” (S.S. Avnesov) and the approach of G.N. Prozumentova, which emphasizes the phenomenon of “personal presence” and the overcoming of the anthropological deficit through the subjectivization of education. The methodological foundation of the study is the information-synergetic approach (I.V. Melik-Gaykazyan), based on the substantiation of the following propositions: 1) the phenomenon of information is an irreversible process; 2) the information process is a mechanism of self-organization; and 3) semiotic forms are the results of stages of the information process. One of the results of this approach was the concept of “semiotic diagnostics” (I.V. Melik-Gaykazyan), the procedures of which make it possible to resolve the problem of measurement in the humanities. The method used is a humanitarian (linguosemiotic) expertise, including discourse analysis and comparative analysis of two cases: Tomsk (Russia) as a historical university center and the Lanzhou New Area (China) as a project for creating a “university-city” from scratch. The material consisted of official narratives and self-descriptions representing educational innovations in these territories. The results of the study showed that the language of educational innovations in both cases functions as a praxeme — an active tool for constructing reality. Universal traits were identified: the university is universally positioned as a “hub,” “driver,” and “bridge,” which visualizes its new active role in the city. Culturally specific differences manifested in the ways of overcoming the “humanitarian deficit.” In Tomsk, the language of innovations (narrative “guardian of traditions and the engine of the future”) is aimed at preserving the humanistic mission of the classical university and rooting innovations in the historical and cultural code. In Lanzhou, the metaphor of the “scientific-educational oasis” and the frames of integration of education and production construct a new identity for the territory and strive to overcome the alienation of the individual from education by including them in solving real development tasks. The study proves that the language of educational innovations is a critically important factor and indicator of the humanitarian quality of transformations within the frameworks of “city-university” concepts. Its analysis not only allows for diagnosing current changes but also for predicting their anthropological consequences, opening perspectives for managing the development of territories not only as technological but also as truly human, meaningful spaces. The proposed tool — humanitarian expertise — allows moving from measuring quantitative effectiveness indicators to analyzing the deep anthropological effects of educational innovations and identifying risks of symbolic dehumanization in “city-university” concepts. Expanding the interpretation of educational innovation to include artificial intelligence infrastructure makes it possible to present universities as active semiotic agents that not only introduce technology into the urban environment, but also create new anthropological meanings in it, thereby overcoming the humanitarian deficit of technocratic development.

items.abstract: This academic article aims to study the meaning and concepts of the Second Royal Working Principle, “Exploding from Within,” analyze the concept of human awareness, and examine the application of this principle in the development of human awareness. The study employs conceptual analysis, philosophical interpretation, and knowledge synthesis derived from the King’s Philosophy, Buddhist philosophy, humanistic psychology, and holistic human development concepts. The findings reveal that the Second Royal Working Principle, “Exploding from Within,” emphasizes strengthening and transformation from within human consciousness before external change occurs. Human awareness is identified as a crucial process enabling individuals to understand themselves, recognize the realities of life, and develop balanced relationships with others and society. Furthermore, the process of developing awareness according to the principle of “Exploding from Within” consists of self-observation, reflective contemplation, intrinsic motivation, and relational transformation. The author synthesizes a new body of knowledge entitled the “I.N.N.E.R. Awareness Conceptual Model,” which represents a framework for developing human awareness from the inner dimension toward external transformation. This model can be applied to enhance quality of life, education, organizational development, and sustainable social development.

items.abstract: This study aimed to examine the current situation, problems, and needs for standard development; develop and evaluate operating standards; and establish the 2025 Situation Awareness Team Operating Standards of the Department of Disease Control. This action research was conducted from January 2025 to February 2026 and comprised five phases: (1) reviewing relevant documents and standards; (2) developing draft standards; (3) pilot testing in three Offices of Disease Prevention and Control; (4) revising the standards based on pilot test findings and expert recommendations; and (5) finalizing the standards. Results: The 2025 Situation Awareness Team Operating Standards of the Department of Disease Control comprised six domains: team establishment, technical capacity, operational readiness, surveillance and situation assessment, quality of outbreak reports, and supporting systems, monitoring, and evaluation. Pilot implementation demonstrated that the participating agencies were able to use the standards for self-assessment. The indicators were clear, reflected actual practice, and helped identify gaps for strengthening the situation awareness system.

items.abstract: Crop rotation farming requires the use of insecticides at multiple stages of the production process, resulting in continuous occupational exposure among farmers. In particular, insecticides that inhibit cholinesterase activity are of significant concern, as decreased blood cholinesterase levels serve as an important biomarker of pesticide exposure and associated health risks. This study aimed to identify factors associated with blood cholinesterase levels related to insecticide exposure among rotational crop farmers in Ban Sa Subdistrict, Chae Hom District, Lampang Province, Thailand. This study included 281 participants, and data were collected between July and September 2025. The research instruments consisted of structured questionnaires assessing knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding the surveillance, prevention, and control of pesticide-related illnesses, as well as a cholinesterase reactive test paper for measuring blood cholinesterase levels. Relationships between variables and blood cholinesterase levels were analyzed using Spearman’s rank correlation coefficient and the Chi-squared test. Predictive factors were subsequently identified using ordinal logistic regression analysis. The results revealed that nine factors were significantly associated with blood cholinesterase levels, including sex, age, educational level, body mass index (BMI), personal hygiene after work, pesticide use per application, average working duration per week, agricultural experience, and the level of surveillance, prevention, and control practices for pesticide-related illnesses. In the multivariable ordinal logistic regression model, four factors significantly associated with blood cholinesterase levels: sex (Adjusted OR=0.52, 95% CI=0.28-0.95), body mass index (Adjusted OR=0.88, 95% CI=0.81-0.96), personal hygiene after work (Adjusted OR=0.31, 95% CI=0.14-0.71), and pesticide use (Adjusted OR=1.28, 95% CI=1.02-1.60). The findings provide empirical evidence to support the planning and implementation of occupational health and safety measures aimed at reducing health risks associated with insecticide exposure among crop rotation farmers.

items.title: “Delivering” Culture Change: A Quality Improvement Approach to Nurse-Resident Relations on Labor & Delivery
items.abstract: Background: Strained nurse-resident relations on Labor and Delivery are a widely recognized but inadequately addressed threat linked to adverse outcomes, trainee and nursing distress, hostile clinical learning environments, and patient safety issues. In our institution, a 2024 Program Evaluation Committee meeting SWOT analysis (Strength-Weakness-Opportunity-Threat) identified nurse-resident relations at a busy academic Labor and Delivery unit as an opportunity for improvement within our residency program. Issues included persistent unprofessional behaviors, inadequate and mistrusted reporting mechanisms, and a culture of silence with a fear of retaliation. Objective: To implement and evaluate a quality improvement model for improving nurse-resident relations on Labor & Delivery. Study Design: Using Kotter’s 8-Step Change Model as a framework, a multidisciplinary quality improvement initiative was launched in May 2024 as a joint effort by resident and nursing leadership. Interventions included creation of an anonymous QR code-based feedback survey, recognition of outstanding nurses and residents, monthly interdisciplinary leadership meetings to review concerns, structured social events, clarification and education regarding resident and nursing escalation pathways, and the establishment of a joint Nurse-Resident Workgroup. Results: In two years, a total of 74 nursing and resident-related incidents were submitted and addressed through the creation of an anonymous QR code-based feedback survey. In the first 7 months there were 26 submissions, in the second 7 months there were 41 submissions, and in the final 7 months there were 7 submissions. QR code submissions declined over time, which served as an indicator of culture improvement. A total of 100 kudos were submitted by both nurses and residents recognizing exemplary interprofessional behavior. Monthly nursing-initiated socials were established at the beginning of each resident rotation to intentionally strengthen camaraderie, promote teamwork, and help nurses and incoming interns build familiarity early in the rotation. As a second phase to the improvement efforts, a Nurse-Resident Workgroup was launched in November 2025, completing six structured meetings by June 2026. This workgroup consisted of a core team of 7 front-line nurses and rotating residents with a total of approximately 10 to 12 participants at each session. This in-person discussion was mediated by combined nursing and residency leadership and focused on conflict resolution and improved situational awareness between both nurses and residents without intensive investment outside of this structured time. Participants were anonymously polled at the fourth and fifth workgroup with 12/12 (100%) positive responses at the fourth workgroup and 9/10 (90%) positive responses at the fifth workgroup, with 0 negative responses in both workgroups. In addition, participants suggested 5 topics for future discussion. Conclusions: A structured and leadership-supported quality improvement initiative can meaningfully improve nurse-resident relationships on Labor and Delivery. The Nurse-Resident Workgroup is a replicable intervention that provides a structured venue for conflict resolution and improved situational awareness between nurses and residents. Discussion allows for understanding of diverse perspectives and roles, which ultimately led to system changes across nursing, residency, and faculty teams. This model provides a framework for other residency programs facing similar challenges and can be adapted to different unique Labor & Delivery environments.

items.title: “The pharmacological potential of CRISPR-Cas9: Revolutionizing gene therapy and drug development”
items.abstract: CRISPR-Cas9 has entered the mainstream of genetic research and therapeutic development, offering a level of programmable and targeted gene editing that has substantially expanded the possibilities of genetic manipulation. This review focuses on the discovery to development of CRISPR-Cas9 and its recent practice in pharmacological and biotechnology field. We discuss further advancements in CRISPR technology such as high-fidelity CRISPR and new systems Cas12 and Cas13 which increases efficiency of editing and opens more opportunities. CRISPR technology has been further advanced when combined with Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning; guide RNA is now optimized while the off-target effects are predicted. The review also focuses on the new targets for therapy, recent trials, the legal and the social and ethical relevance of the CRISPR approach. With the development of CRISPR-Cas9 promising and revolutionary preliminary achievements in the fields of drug development and disease management and tissue engineering are anticipated. Although, in its application, there are questions that have been raised concerning side effects, carriers, and ethics, it is important to take advantage of it in the right manner. As seen in this review, CRISPR-Cas9 plays the crucial part of the development of biomedical studies and therapeutic paradigms.

items.title: 29. Introducing Data Science Concepts to Animal Science Graduate Students Through Application-based Learning.
items.abstract: Abstract The rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and data science into biological research has created a growing need for computational literacy among graduate students in life science disciplines. However, many students’ entering biology-related graduate programs have limited formal training in programming, statistics, or machine learning, creating a significant barrier to engaging with modern data-driven research. The objective of this study was to evaluate baseline perceptions of AI and data science among animal science students prior to participating in a course introducing these concepts through application-based learning. A pre-course perception survey was administered to students enrolled in an introductory AI and data science course in animal science (n = 10). Survey questions used a 5-point Likert scale to assess prior programming experience, familiarity with AI concepts, attitudes toward AI applications in animal science and motivation to learn these skills. Students reported limited prior experience with programming languages (mean = 2.9 ± 1.45) and moderate use of AI tools in daily life (mean = 2.98 ± 1.32). Despite limited technical exposure, students indicated moderate understanding of basic AI and data science concepts (mean = 3.6 ± 0.70 and 3.6 ± 0.52, respectively). Participants expressed strong agreement that AI and data science can be effectively applied in animal science (mean = 3.9 ± 0.57) and that learning these skills would benefit their academic or professional development (mean = 4.0 ± 0.67). Students also expressed moderate motivation to learn AI applications in livestock systems (mean = 3.5 ± 1.08). While this project provides the current perceptions of students and their skill levels in AI and data science, a follow-up post survey to assess the effects of such a course, and combining it with a Mann-Whiteney U test will further inform the required pedagogical shifts. These preliminary findings highlight the value of interdisciplinary teaching approaches that integrate biological applications with computational methods (such as an AI in animal science course) and may inform curriculum design for graduate programs seeking to prepare life science students for increasingly data-intensive research environments.

items.title: 367. Multi-modal Machine Learning for the Early Detection of Subclinical Ketosis in Dairy Cattle.
items.abstract: Abstract Subclinical ketosis (SCK) is a prevalent metabolic disorder in transition dairy cows causing significant economic and welfare impacts, yet early detection remains challenging due to absent clinical signs and disease complexity. Two complementary projects developed multi-modal machine learning systems for prepartum prediction of postpartum SCK risk. The first integrated depth image-derived body shape features (extracted via CNN, anatomical keypoint sampling, and CNN-RNN), wearable sensor behavioral data, cow history, and text embeddings from farm management notes using generic and fine-tuned LLMs; Random Forest models combining image and tabular data achieved F₁ = 0.706, with fine-tuned LLM text embeddings further improving sensor-based models (F₁ 0.681 vs. 0.655). The second project added genomic data (78,964 SNPs reduced to 128 dimensions via UMAP) and introduced a cloud-based modular pipeline for automated image processing and data integration; among three fusion strategies tested, late fusion achieved the highest performance (F₁ up to 0.750) for binary SCK classification. Together, these projects show that integrating phenomic and genomic data through modern machine learning and fusion techniques substantially improves early SCK detection, supporting preventive health management in dairy farms.

items.title: 4D-PRINTED SHAPE-MEMORY POLYMERS FOR ADVANCED DRUG DELIVERY: PROGRAMMING, STIMULI-RESPONSIVE MECHANISMS AND BIOMEDICAL APPLICATIONS
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Four-dimensional (4D) printing is an emerging additive manufacturing technology that integrates three-dimensional (3D) printing with smart materials capable of undergoing programmed changes in shape or function over time in response to specific stimuli. This technology has attracted increasing interest in pharmaceutical drug delivery because it offers the possibility of developing dynamic, programmable, and personalized drug-delivery systems. This review provides an overview of the fundamental principles of 4D printing, including stimulus-responsive mechanisms, smart materials, and major printing technologies relevant to pharmaceutical applications. Particular emphasis is placed on shape-memory polymers, hydrogels, and other responsive materials that can respond to temperature, moisture, pH, light, magnetic fields, and other environmental stimuli. Recent applications in gastroretentive, esophageal, intravesical, intestinal, transdermal, implantable, and localized drug-delivery systems are discussed, with emphasis on their potential to improve drug retention, controlled release, site-specific therapy, minimally invasive administration, and personalized treatment. The major advantages and challenges associated with pharmaceutical 4D printing are also critically evaluated, including biocompatibility, drug–material compatibility, drug stability, reproducibility, quality control, manufacturing cost, scalability, long-term material stability, regulatory requirements, and clinical translation. Finally, future perspectives involving biodegradable smart materials, multi-material printing, nanotechnology, artificial intelligence, and personalized medicine are highlighted. Overall, 4D printing represents a promising approach for transforming conventional static dosage forms into dynamic and adaptive drug-delivery systems; however, comprehensive in-vitro, in-vivo, manufacturing, regulatory, and clinical studies are required to establish its safety, reproducibility, and therapeutic effectiveness. Keywords: 4D Printing, Shape Memory Polymers, Smart Drug Delivery, Stimuli-Responsive Materials, Personalized Medicine.

items.title: 93. Smartbreeder: A Data-driven Virtual Assistant to Support Nellore Sire Selection Accounting for Genotype-by-environment-by-management Interactions.
items.abstract: Abstract The enviromics approach has emerged as an efficient framework for modeling genotype-by-environment-by-management (GxExM) interactions in animal breeding. It characterizes environmental conditions (ECs) in which animals are raised using detailed environmental and management data, providing a biologically meaningful representation of environmental variability for more reliable genetic evaluation and selection of better-adapted animals. Nonetheless, the implementation of enviromics in breeding programs presents two major challenges: (i) the recurrent collection of dynamic management information from producers and (ii) the translation of multiple expected progeny differences (EPDs), estimated for each sire across ECs, into practical recommendations. To address these challenges, we developed SmartBreeder, a virtual assistant that helps Nellore producers across Brazil identify sires best suited to their local climate and soil conditions, management practices, and breeding goals. SmartBreeder was developed as a web application using TypeScript, React, and Vite for the frontend, and Supabase for backend services, with PostgreSQL for data storage and Edge Functions for server-side processing. The system follows a three-step workflow: (i) collection of environmental and management information using a structured online survey, (ii) classification of the EC based on the surveyed farm profile, and (iii) recommendation of Nellore sires with their EPDs for the predicted EC. The survey includes four sections covering general information, soil management, supplemental feeding strategies, and reproductive management. A Supabase Edge Function receives twenty-two variables from the survey and queries a large language model (Gemini 2.5) via prompt engineering with few-shot learning. The prompt incorporates a training dataset of 60 farms to assign the surveyed farm profile to one of two ECs: an intensive production system (ENV1) or an extensive production system (ENV2). The predicted EC is then used to query a PostgreSQL database containing EPDs and accuracy estimates for Nellore sires in both ECs, obtained from GxExM genetic evaluations for yearling weight, scrotal circumference, age at first calving, ribeye area, fat thickness, and marbling. The platform also highlights top-ranking sires for each trait and provides complementary information (inbreeding coefficient, pedigree, and year of birth). SmartBreeder demonstrates the potential of a virtual assistant to collect high-resolution environmental and management data directly from producers and to translate multiple EPDs from GxExM genetic evaluations into practical sire recommendations through a user-friendly interface. By integrating the enviromics approach, the platform enables ECs to be assigned independently of phenotypic records, allowing sire recommendations based on GxExM models to be extended to future years and even to farms beyond the original breeding program. This approach increases the potential impact of optimized management and precision breeding across the broader cattle population. Future deployment as Android and iOS applications will enhance accessibility and on-farm adoption. SmartBreeder, developed for Nellore cattle in Brazil, can be adapted to other breeds and regions worldwide.

items.title: A cognitive hierarchy-guided abstract forest knowledge base based on cognitive load theory
items.abstract: The Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) framework mitigates hallucination issues arising from questions beyond its knowledge boundaries by retrieving relevant knowledge to expand the knowledge scope of Large Language Models (LLMs). However, as the cognitive agent in the question-answering process, the RAG framework overlooks the implicit knowledge demands in complex questions, leading to a decline in the recall rate of pertinent knowledge. Furthermore, existing RAG frameworks neglect the intricate relationships among knowledge entries in the knowledge base, resulting in their reasoning processes lacking effective knowledge support. These issues indicate that the RAG framework may be misaligned with Cognitive Load Theory proposed by John Sweller during the cognitive process, thereby introducing additional cognitive load that hinder effective reasoning. To address these problems, we propose a Cognitive Hierarchy-Guided Abstract Forest Knowledge Base (CH-AFKB) based on Cognitive Load Theory. This approach conceptualizes knowledge in unstructured knowledge bases to expand the implicit knowledge within the existing knowledge base content. It also iteratively constructs an abstract forest knowledge base with ”concept-instance” characteristics from the bottom up to model relationships among knowledge entries. In experiments across three downstream tasks, the RAG framework with CH-AFKB demonstrated superior performance in most scenarios compared to strong baselines. Compared to existing RAG and LLM baselines, the CH-AFKB exhibited remarkable advantages in retrieval efficiency, knowledge integrity, and factual consistency.

items.title: A Comprehensive Review of Strategies to Enhance Quality and Safety in Infertility Laboratories.
items.abstract: Assisted reproductive technology (ART) laboratories are complex environments in which human gametes and embryos are handled through highly sensitive procedures. Because of procedural complexity, manual documentation, high workload and the need for precise identification at ev-ery step, these laboratories are inherently vulnerable to er-rors that may compromise patient safety, clinical outcomes and confidence in ART. Potential hazards may arise from equipment malfunction, human error, environmental insta-bility or deviation from validated procedures. Therefore, a comprehensive framework for risk assessment, risk man-agement and safety monitoring is essential. This review dis-cusses the main risk factors in ART laboratories and exam-ines established mitigation strategies, including witnessing systems, process mapping, key performance indicators and quality management systems. It also summarizes recom-mended procedures and case-based evidence for improving laboratory safety and performance. Current evidence indi-cates that proactive risk assessment, electronic witnessing, emerging artificial intelligence tools and strict adherence to international guidelines can reduce the likelihood of errors and support high-quality, safe patient care.

items.title: A Dual Task Learning Framework for Multitype Bridge Condition Assessment Using UAV Imagery
items.abstract: Abstract Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery combined with artificial intelligence offers unprecedented potential to improve bridge health monitoring, reducing reliance on labor-intensive and potentially hazardous manual inspections. However, the diversity of bridge types and damage categories poses significant challenges for existing convolutional neural network (CNN)-based methods, which often focus on single damage types or specific bridge structures, limiting their generalization and comprehensive applicability. To address these limitations, this study proposes a novel dual task deep learning framework, termed bridge damage detection network (BDDNet), for simultaneous detection and segmentation of multiple surface damages across various bridge types using UAV imagery. BDDNet integrates a global attention module (GAM) within its backbone to capture long-range dependencies and enhance multiscale feature representation. Additionally, a novel APC2f module based on pinwheel convolution is incorporated into the detection branch, enlarging the receptive field and refining feature learning for small and complex damages. Extensive experiments conducted on a multitype bridge data set demonstrate that BDDNet achieves high performance, attaining approximately 85% mean average precision (mAP) in damage detection and 82% mean intersection over union (mIoU) in segmentation. Visual results further confirm the model’s ability to accurately identify and delineate diverse damages, such as rust, missing bolts, cracks, and spalling, even in complex environments with limited training data. Overall, the proposed BDDNet provides an efficient, generalizable, and practical solution for UAV-based bridge inspection, enabling comprehensive structural condition assessment and laying the foundation for future quantitative damage evaluation.

items.title: A Fatigue-Gated Hold on Outbound Messages: A Technical Note for Communication-Platform-as-a-Service (CPaaS) Systems
items.abstract: When a person approves an action while tired, the AI agent that carries it out may send a message that cannot be taken back, a refund, an alert, an account change. This note suggests a simple fix: before sending, check if the approving person showed signs of fatigue. If so, hold the message briefly for a second look before it goes out. This applies to any communication platform that sends such messages on behalf of a human or an AI agent, including Zoho CPaaS, Twilio, and Infobip.

items.title: A foundation model for energy and radiation systems built on heterogeneous scientific interfaces
items.abstract: Scientific foundation models are commonly evaluated after heterogeneous physical problems have already been translated into a compatible gridded, tokenized or symbolic representation. This leaves the scientific interface outside both the pretrained model and the audit of what is actually reused. We study the complementary setting in which boundary histories, sparse monitor records and loading histories retain their native inference classes and their outputs remain on Cartesian, latitude-longitude and unstructured domains. GEODE couples task-specific scientific interfaces to a shared routed library of wavelet operators. A single jointly pretrained model represents cavity flow, radiation dose and elastoplastic stress, then acquires a heat exchanger and a reactor subchannel by training a private interface containing 2.1% of its parameters. Earlier predictions remain unchanged by parameter isolation, whereas unrestricted fine-tuning degrades them by factors of 14-29. Crucially, preservation alone does not establish reuse: norm-matched randomized-library controls show that the contribution of pretrained computation is conditional on the task and data regime. A separate decomposition shows that full-field relative L2 error can substantially understate error relative to spatial variation when field level dominates the norm. Task-specific operators remain more accurate on three of the five problems. These results distinguish multi-task coverage, preservation and pretrained reuse as separate properties that must be tested independently when scientific foundation models span heterogeneous interfaces.

items.title: A Framework for Building Resilience with Adaptive Leadership and AI Readiness in Contemporary South Asian Organizations
items.abstract: While AI is often viewed as a strategic resource for improving efficiency and competitiveness, its outcomes remain uneven across organizations. Limited conceptual clarity remains regarding how artificial intelligence adoption contributes to organizational resilience, particularly in turbulent South Asian contexts. This paper argues that the missing link lies in AI readiness, conceptualized as a multidimensional capability that reflects the extent to which organizations and their employees are prepared to adopt, use, and adapt to AI technologies. Based on an integrative review, the study draws on the Resource-Based View, dynamic capabilities theory, and leadership perspectives to develop a conceptual framework that positions AI readiness as a mediating mechanism between leadership and organizational resilience. Leadership is conceptualized as an enabling force that shapes organizational conditions and supports capability development, while AI readiness facilitates the translation of technological potential into adaptive capacity. Organizational resilience is viewed as a dynamic capability involving anticipation, coping, and adaptation under disruption. The study further situates this framework within the context of South Asian economies characterized by institutional volatility, resource constraints, and uneven digital maturity. It argues that under such conditions, leadership-enabled AI readiness becomes particularly critical for sustaining organizational performance. The paper contributes to theory by integrating leadership, AI readiness, and resilience within a capability-based framework and offers practical insights for organizations seeking to navigate technological change in turbulent environments.

items.title: A Generative AI-Based Framework for Decision Making in B2C E-Commerce: Conceptualization and Pilot Study
items.abstract: Decision making in business-to-consumer (B2C) e-commerce connects company and consumer activities before, during and after purchase. Existing generative artificial intelligence (GAI) applications usually address isolated tasks. This article develops a conceptual framework in which the five-stage Consumer Buying Behaviour (CBB) process structures GAI-assisted decisions. It links need clarification, information gathering, feasible-offer comparison, transaction review and post-purchase assessment in a recursive cycle with decision gates and bounded support functions. To illustrate its measurement and reporting procedure, five employees and three consumers completed baseline tasks followed by intended-to-be-comparable prompt-guided cases. No integrated GAI system, autonomous agent, live data connection or consequential transaction was implemented. The questionnaire items are descriptive indicators, not validated latent constructs, and findings are limited to participant-specific summaries. Several rubric-based and self-reported values were numerically more favourable in the second condition, but the fixed order prevents separation of prompt support from practice, familiarity, novelty, fatigue or expectancy effects. Technical accuracy, trust calibration, automation bias, commercial impact and post-purchase outcomes were not evaluated. The pilot is a procedural illustration and design input; it does not validate the framework or establish effectiveness. Larger randomized or counterbalanced studies using validated measures, task-level records and implemented-system tests are required.

items.title: A Human-in-the-Loop Machine Learning Approach for Stress Ribbon Bridge Cable Profiling
items.abstract: Stress ribbon bridges (SRBs) create unique design challenges resulting from their extreme flexibility and the strong coupling between the forces in the cable and the deck. This paper presents the development of a Python-based interactive tool, to allow the rapid estimation of primary cable sag profiles in SRBs using traditional analytical formulations and artificial intelligence (AI). The tool combines parabolic cable sag equations, cable mechanics in catenary terms, load-span-sag-tension relationships, and a Machine Learning (ML) subcomponent. The AI module, including a Random Forest regressor, was initially trained using 103 real bridge data. The artificial intelligence module is fine tuned to the user through the iterative process of defining a task, predicting the sag, and then providing feedback to improve the regression module for the next analysis. The methodology is discussed, including derivations of the mathematical formulation of the traditional cable mechanics and design constraints. The paper describes the architecture of the AI module, key geometric and material inputs, the training process and the feedback and retraining workflow. Initial analysis shows a root mean square error up to 0.27 meter, which improved by approximately 33% to 0.18 meter after incorporating user feedback, successfully correcting systematic biases in various load cases. Tool illustrates the potential for machine learning to enhance structural engineering design by delivering fast sag estimates that adapt across user interactions, and will ultimately reduce the number of repetitive analysis cycles.

items.title: A LAYERED REFERENCE FRAMEWORK FOR SCALABLE DATA ENGINEERING AND AI APPLICATIONS
items.abstract: Modern organizations depend on data platforms that must serve two audiences at once: analytical workloads that expect consistent, well-governed tables, and artificial intelligence (AI) workloads that expect fresh, versioned, feature-ready data delivered to training and inference systems. Most platforms were not designed for both, and scaling one audience often degrades the other. This paper consolidates established results from the systems and machine learning literature into a layered reference framework for data engineering platforms that scale across volume, velocity, workload diversity, and change. The framework organizes responsibilities into ingestion, storage, processing, feature and model, and serving layers, bound together by cross-cutting schema contracts, quality gates, lineage, and observability. Seven design principles are derived from established systems literature: separating storage from compute, declarative pipeline definitions, idempotent and replayable processing, explicit schema contracts, incremental computation, unified batch and streaming semantics, and automated validation gates. The paper then shows how the same framework supports AI applications through training data management, feature pipelines, model serving feedback loops, and retrieval-augmented applications. An analytical comparison of lambda, kappa, and lakehouse-based architectures against the stated requirements is provided, followed by a discussion of open challenges including cost governance, semantic drift, and the operational burden of unstructured data. The resulting framework provides a vendor-neutral architectural blueprint that systematically connects scalability requirements, platform responsibilities, operational controls, and AI lifecycle needs, enabling engineering teams to evaluate and evolve data and AI platforms incrementally.

items.title: A Machine Learning Framework for Flood Risk Assessment With Imbalanced Data
items.abstract: ABSTRACT This study presents a machine‐learning framework for identifying areas of elevated flood risk using imbalanced, high‐dimensional geospatial datasets. Using the Mandra River Basin in Greece as a case study, an extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) classifier was trained on 11 flood‐related features including hydrological, meteorological, soil and topographic data, whereas 454 geolocated citizens' emergency calls were used as target information. Class imbalance was addressed through a weighted‐only strategy to preserve the integrity of the original dataset, while adjusting class contributions during the training process. Bayesian optimization and stratified 10‐fold cross‐validation were combined to tune and evaluate the model performance. Threshold‐sweep analysis enables the identification of multiple operational settings based on precision–recall trade‐offs and cost‐sensitive criteria. The results revealed physically interpretable feature importance patterns, with terrain elevation (TE) (45%) and accumulated rainfall (25%) emerging as the dominant predictors according to feature importance analysis, followed by curve number (16%) and the Manning coefficient (9.2%). The proposed framework provides a reliable, data‐driven tool for flood risk assessment, and supports a flexible, two‐tier decision strategy that differentiates between emergency escalation and broader situational awareness.

items.title: A Peircean framework for explainable and human-centred artificial intelligence
items.abstract: This article develops a philosophical-conceptual framework for rethinking Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) and Human-Centred Artificial Intelligence (HCAI) through the pragmatic semiotics of Charles Sanders Peirce. Rather than treating explainability solely as algorithmic transparency, the article conceptualizes it as a socially situated epistemic process through which AI-generated outputs are interpreted, evaluated, contested, and revised within human practices of inquiry. Drawing on Peirce’s concepts of semiosis, abduction, inquiry, fallibilism, pragmaticism, and the community of inquiry, the framework distinguishes between computational processes performed by AI systems and the human and institutional practices through which their outputs acquire epistemic and practical significance. AI outputs may function as signs and may generate hypotheses that are functionally analogous to abductive possibilities; however, interpretation, evidential assessment, justification, ethical judgment, and responsibility remain situated within human communities of inquiry. The framework further translates Peircean concepts into practical principles for XAI, including contextual interpretation, uncertainty communication, contestability, human review, stakeholder participation, evidence-based revision, and continuous evaluation. A worked example involving generative AI illustrates how an AI-generated explanation can move through interpretation, questioning, evidence checking, contestation, and revision rather than being accepted as a final epistemic product. The article therefore positions Peircean pragmatism not as a replacement for technical XAI methods but as a philosophical and normative framework that complements them by clarifying the epistemological conditions of meaningful explanation, trustworthy human oversight, and responsible AI governance.

items.title: A Person‐Environment Fit Framework for Measuring Multi‐Risk Community Resilience: 24 Indicators with Metrics and Vulnerability Thresholds
items.abstract: ABSTRACT This study addresses a persistent challenge in community resilience research and practice: how to assess and build resilience when communities face multiple, interacting, and potentially unforeseen risks. It develops a relational framework for multi‐risk resilience based on Person–Environment (P–E) Fit Theory. The study conceptualizes community resilience as emerging at the intersection of three interrelated determinants: Knowledge about self and the environment, Assets (natural, built, social) in the environment, and Support Services that address gaps between Knowledge and Assets. Risk and vulnerability arise or intensify where relationships among Knowledge, Assets and Support Services are poorly aligned, while resilience is strengthened through their mutually reinforcing alignment. One‐Risk concept is introduced in this study as providing a common relational layer for examining how this alingnment conditions different risk configurations. The framework is operationalized through SCORE (Stakeholder Co‐Creation and Review), an original co‐creation methodology simulating co‐creative resilience and combining stakeholder agency, peer review, quantitative agreement thresholding, and defined decision rights. Six stakeholders representing different sectors and multi‐risk contexts across the UK, India, USA, China, and South Africa initially proposed 54 interrelating indicators under the three determinants. Following peer review and an 80% agreement threshold for retention, 24 indicators were retained: five Knowledge (e.g., situation awareness index), 13 Assets (e.g., protective nature index), and six Support Services (e.g., resilience planning index) indicators. Each indicator is accompanied by a measurement metric and provisional vulnerability threshold. Their main contribution lies in their relational organization through the One‐Risk framework to reveal potential P‐E mismatches and support the development of relational resilience profiles. The resulting framework encourages a shift from asking whether a community possesses sufficient resilience attributes to asking where mismatches between community abilities, environmental conditions, and support services generate vulnerability, and which mutually reinforcing interventions can reduce those mismatches across multiple risk configurations. This is the principal basis on which this study extends the existing literature on multi‐risk resilience.

items.title: A pilot study of rifle and head kinematics during 0.50 caliber rifle firing
items.abstract: Introduction This study analysed rifle and head kinematics during firing, using automated motion tracking to quantify maximum rifle displacement, head displacement, and head acceleration. Methods Six professional snipers participated in repeated firing trials under controlled conditions. Additional trials were performed for selected participants to show recoil conditions without a muzzle brake. Results Rifle displacement ranged from 36.30 to 67.65 mm and head displacement from 25.86 to 44.55 mm with the muzzle break, whereas without the muzzle brake values increased substantially to 76.36–102.97 mm and 76.47–82.47 mm, respectively. Peak head acceleration showed a less consistent pattern, ranging from 3.71 to 8.62 g with the muzzle brake and 5.10–8.71 g without it. Interindividual variability was observed across all measures, suggesting an influence of participant-specific biomechanical and anthropometric characteristics on recoil transmission. Discussion The findings from this pilot study indicate that the use of a muzzlebrake may reduce the translational recoil motion of both the rifle and theshooter, whereas peak head acceleration appears to be less affected. However, as the condition without a muzzle break was evaluated in only two participants with a limited number of trials, these observations should be considered preliminary and descriptive rather than conclusive. The results also suggest that individual biomechanical factors may influence recoil response, highlighting the need for larger, balanced studies to better understand the effects of muzzle brakes and their potential implications for ergonomics and shooting performance optimisation.

items.title: A policy framework for ethical research assessment in the digital age
items.abstract: This policy framework sets out the values, principles, and human rights that should govern research assessment as data and artificial intelligence change both the research being assessed and the means of assessing it. It is deliverable 2.1 of Workstream 2 of CoARA-ERIP. The framework grounds research assessment in the human right to science and the rights connected with it, names six values that the CoARA-ERIP community holds in common, and derives from them twelve principles, among them human judgement, evidence mapping in place of ranking, contestability, the recognition of a plurality of contributions, and the openness of research information. It identifies the commitments that fall to research-performing organisations, research-funding organisations, evaluators, researchers, infrastructure providers, and policymakers; distinguishes uses of artificial intelligence in assessment that may be supported, that require particular care, and that are not appropriate; and sets out how the framework is implemented, monitored, and reviewed. The companion deliverables, the framework for assessing digital contributions (2.2) and the methodological guidelines (2.3), carry the framework into method and instruments.

items.title: A Preliminary Study of Motivational Interviewing Training Using a Large Language Model (ChatGPT): Effects on Empathy and Motivational Interviewing Confidence among Social Work Students
items.abstract: Background: Motivational interviewing (MI) requires repeated practice, individualized feedback, and ongoing coaching that shortterm group education cannot sufficiently provide. Large language models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT may offer realistic conversational simulation and immediate feedback. This pilot study examined whether an LLM (ChatGPT)–integrated MI training program improves empathy and MI Confidence among social work students.Methods: A one-group repeated measures quasi-experimental design was applied to 15 undergraduate social welfare students. The four-session program used ChatGPT (GPT-5.5) as a virtual client for open-ended questions, affirmations, reflective listening, and summaries (OARS) practice with automated Motivational Interviewing Treatment Integrity-based feedback. Empathy, MI Skill Confidence, and Global Interviewing Confidence were measured at pretest, posttest, and 4-week follow-up, and analyzed using Friedman and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. Qualitative content analysis of participants’ experiences was also conducted.Results: Empathy improved significantly across time points (χ2=6.037, P=0.049), increasing from pretest to posttest (P=0.014) and remaining higher at follow-up (P=0.037). MI Skill Confidence showed an upward trend without statistical significance (χ2=2.561, P=0.278). Global Interviewing Confidence changed significantly (χ2=6.682, P=0.035), being higher at follow-up than pretest (P=0.021). Qualitative analysis yielded four themes: realistic simulation, immediate feedback, skill mastery through repeated practice, and requests for enhanced realism.Conclusions: An LLM (ChatGPT)–integrated MI training program may improve empathy and overall interviewing confidence and function as an effective auxiliary tool complementing traditional MI education. LLMs can support learners’ repeated practice and immediate feedback.

items.title: A Proposed Rubric for Evaluating Expressed Clinical Reasoning in Large Language Model Responses
items.abstract: We propose a rubric for assessing expressed clinical reasoning in model responses, drawing on three bodies of work: medical education assessment frameworks (ART, SCT, Key Feature Problems and OSCE); clinical LLM benchmarks (MedR-Bench, HealthBench, TIMER-Bench, DR. BENCH, PrIME-LLM and PatientSafeBench); and general LLM reasoning evaluation research, including the Factuality-Validity-Coherence-Utility taxonomy, FaithCoT-Bench and C2-Faith. We use groundedness as a clinically oriented adaptation of the taxonomy's factuality category. The rubric brings these concepts together in a multidimensional framework for scoring free-text responses to gold-standard clinical vignettes. It includes provisional behavioural anchors, applicability rules and a separate flag for case-specific safety-critical errors. General-domain frameworks inform its design but are not treated as validated clinical instruments. The rubric does not replace case-specific reference criteria or the task-specific metrics of existing benchmarks. It has not yet been tested for inter-rater reliability, construct validity or clinical utility. Its immediate purpose is to make evaluation decisions explicit and open to scrutiny before empirical testing.

items.title: A Study for Understanding Consumer Behaviour Using AI in Marketing Management
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is slowly changing the boundaries of marketing management in the form of decoding consumer behavior supported by data driven methods as well as a hyper level of customization. The research being conducted currently is mainly aimed at studying the path of transformation in consumer behavior starting with the traditional methods of surveying and intuition to the AI-driven sophisticated framework using the tracking data on a real-time profile. In addition, it seeks to know the implications of strategic AI technologies like natural language processing (NLP), machine learning (ML) and computer vision with the view to predict trends, understanding customer emotions and boost retail sales. The most important thrust areas are the possibilities of AI in analyzing psychological and emotional indicators based on affective computing placing more significance on the ethical issues. Combining real life examples and insights supported by visualizations in the form of figures and tables created with the help of Python, a more realistic layer has been brought into the study in question highlighting the importance of the AI in the field of marketing. Moreover, this paper is mainly concerned with the application of AI in the sphere of marketing management. This has been done after considering a number of factors including ethical issues, data privacy and more significantly, the appropriate balance of personalization and rights of the consumer.

items.title: A Survey on Resource Scheduling and Optimization for Space‑Air‑Ground Integrated Communication‑Sensing‑Computation Networks
items.abstract: The development of sixth generation (6G) communications is aimed at achieving global connectivity, covering oceans and remote areas with limited ground infrastructure. With the integration of sensing, communication and computing (ISCC) technology, the space-air-ground integrated network (SAGIN) is evolving from a simple data transmission channel to an intelligent task processing platform. This paper uses a narrative review method to analyze the evolution path of resource orchestration technology in heterogeneous environments, and focuses on mathematical programming and data-driven intelligent methods to optimize resources. The existing research is classified according to the method system. This paper also examines the architecture paradigm, multi-dimensional resource modeling and algorithm system. Studies have shown that static methods such as Lagrangian dual decomposition and block coordinate descent provide the necessary performance benchmarks, and deep reinforcement learning can achieve fast response in high mobility links. In addition, this paper discusses the potential of large language model (LLM) as a semantic interpreter, which can accelerate the process of parsing task requirements into technical constraints in specific applications. This study provides a methodological reference for achieving task-centered connectivity, and believes that a hybrid framework that combines the accuracy of deterministic methods and the adaptability of learning methods is a feasible development direction for future space infrastructure.

items.title: A Systematic Review of Artificial Intelligence-Supported Physics Education in Developing Countries: Implications for Sustainable Development Goals 4 and 10
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming educational landscapes worldwide, with applications ranging from intelligent tutoring systems and adaptive learning platforms to automated assessment and personalized feedback mechanisms. In physics education specifically, AI-supported tools have demonstrated potential to enhance conceptual understanding, problem-solving skills, and student engagement by providing individualized learning pathways and real-time diagnostic feedback. However, the integration of AI in education remains highly uneven across global contexts. While developed countries possess the infrastructure, resources, and institutional capacity to implement AI-supported learning at scale, developing countries face persistent challenges including limited digital infrastructure, inadequate teacher training, and constrained educational budgets. The COVID-19 pandemic exacerbated these disparities, revealing profound gaps in educational technology access and preparedness. SDG 4 (Quality Education) calls for ensuring inclusive and equitable quality education and promoting lifelong learning opportunities for all. Target 4.4 specifically emphasizes increasing the number of youth and adults with relevant skills, including ICT skills . SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities) aims to reduce inequality within and among countries, with Target 10.2 emphasizing the social, economic, and political inclusion of all . The intersection of AI-supported physics education and these two SDGs represents a critical yet underexplored research area. While AI has the potential to democratize access to high-quality physics instruction—particularly in regions facing teacher shortages—it may also exacerbate existing inequalities if deployment is uneven or culturally inappropriate. A systematic synthesis of existing evidence is necessary to understand what works, for whom, and under what conditions. This review addresses a significant gap: no comprehensive systematic review currently exists that synthesizes evidence on AI-supported physics education specifically in developing country contexts with explicit attention to equity and inclusion outcomes.

items.title: A Three-Layer Framework for Measuring Names and Its Census Application on a Token Launchpad
items.abstract: Asset names influence market behavior, yet standardized name measurement remains lacking. Existing processing fluency measures focus mainly on alphabetic languages and are unsuitable for Chinese names. Cultural meanings usually require manual coding, limiting large-scale analysis, while name competition through reuse and semantic crowding remains underexplored. This study constructs a dataset of 513,647 naming attempts from the Four token launchpad on BNB Chain between February and June 2026 and proposes a three-layer framework for name measurement. The form layer measures linguistic fluency using 38 Chinese-oriented features. The reference layer captures cultural meanings through human coding and large language model expansion with reliability evaluation. The relation layer measures name reuse, semantic crowding, and lexical variation. The three layers are largely independent, with correlations below 0.11. Census analysis reveals that name diversity follows Heaps' law, new-name adoption declines over time, name reuse shows heavy-tailed patterns, and repeated naming occurs at distinct creator-level and cross-creator time scales. Cultural events also trigger rapid naming responses. The framework, annotated dataset, and code are released to support scalable analysis of naming behavior in digital markets and other naming environments.

items.title: A Three–Dimensional Conceptual Framework of Workplace Learning: Integrating Supervisor Support, Peer Support, and Reflective Practice
items.abstract: Workplace learning is an important part of vocational education, yet its conceptualization remains varied across studies. Such variation makes it difficult to compare findings and explain how learning develops across workplace contexts. This paper therefore develops a three-dimensional framework of workplace learning centered on supervisor support, peer support, and reflective practice. Drawing on workplace learning theory and relevant empirical and theoretical literature, the framework brings together two social dimensions of learning and a reflective dimension through which students interpret and learn from workplace experience. Supervisor support provides guidance and developmental feedback, peer support facilitates informal interaction and collaborative learning, and reflective practice enables students to review experience and inform subsequent action. Bringing these three components together provides a clearer basis for examining student learning in authentic work settings and for designing workplace learning in technical and vocational education and training. The framework also provides a basis for future empirical testing across different educational and workplace contexts.
